rules.why: A token of the build's own informers that a poll sends back; each build has its own and no screen shows it.
When this build filled its own minute of the answer; the two builds fill theirs moments apart.
OpenCost's window runs up to the moment a build filled its minute of the answer, and so do the costs and efficiencies over it. number-check-cost.spec.ts holds these numbers to OpenCost.
The cluster's metrics at the moment each build asked, kept for its own moments. number-check-monitoring.spec.ts holds them to the Prometheus.
The dev image is built WITH_CLAUDE_CODE and the compared release tag is the one without it, not a difference in the code.
Every lease's holder renews it every few seconds; whether a renewal falls inside a build's first live frame is timing, so one build's frame can hold a lease twice and count one more.

A lease's holder renews it on a timer: kube-apiserver its identity lease and the kubelet its node's lease every 10 seconds, Kyverno its kyverno-health lease, and leader election (kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, Kyverno's controllers) every 2 seconds. A build's first live frame stays open up to 15 seconds, so how many renewals fall inside it is timing, and one build's frames can hold a lease's events past the other build's last. Only those events are taken, whole, and only while all three frames hold the lease's first event; an event both builds' frames hold is still compared cell by cell, and so is a lease one frame lacks.

GET /ai/model-configs/uses is new: it says which model config answers alert investigations, Investigate now and Optimization, and why (docs/features.md "Which model answers what"). v0.7.9 has no GET there and answers 405.
The detail of v0.7.9's 405 answer, Method Not Allowed, which the new route does not send.
The new route's answer: one row per use (alert investigations, Investigate now, Optimization) with its choice and the config that answers it.

GPU metrics read dcgm-exporter 4.9.0's metric names beside the earlier ones. The kind dev install's stand-in exporter (deploy/kind/gpu-metrics.yaml) serves two of its four GPUs under the 4.9.0 names, which v0.7.9 does not read: the GPU count, the memory totals and the list's length and order count those two.
The rows of the two GPUs the stand-in exporter serves under dcgm-exporter 4.9.0's names, which v0.7.9 does not read.
